style.vernacular: Sudano-Sahelian capital on the Niger: ordinary buildings are 1-3 storey cement-block and rendered-concrete houses and shophouses in earth ochre, cream and laterite red with flat roofs or rusting corrugated-iron sheets, set behind high compound walls on red-earth streets. Colonial-era administrative blocks are cream/ochre rendered; the 1970s onward adds Arabian-style concrete (Grand Mosque) and Neo-Sudanese towers such as the 20-storey BCEAO tower. Mango, neem and kapok-type shade trees and dust everywhere in the dry season.
style.ornament: Neo-Sudanese motifs on prestige buildings (tapering buttressed towers, conical pinnacles, projecting toron beams) after the Djenne and Timbuktu mosques; plain painted render with arched openings on colonial blocks; bright hand-painted shopfront signs and tailors' boards in the markets.

sources.what: Koppen Aw savanna climate; BCEAO tower classed as Neo-Sudanic modelled on Djenne/Timbuktu mosques; Cite administrative 2003-2010; National Museum is a cemented structure based on traditional Malian designs; airport opened 1974
mudbrick/adobe plaster, toron beams, conical pinnacles, tapering buttresses, red or white plaster, Neo-Sudanese revival 1906-1935
Saudi-funded 1974-76 mosque, two concrete minarets of Arabian-peninsula look, earlier mud-brick mosque on the site
